rationale: This is an equal-weight rank blend of two well-documented published anomalies (book-to-market and net repurchase/payout yield) with no genuine interaction — SUMRANK is additive, so it cannot test the stated "double-confirmation" conditioning story and amounts to a trivial rediscovery.

The sign flip mechanically places expensive net issuers (very negative z-score × −1) in the long leg, which directly contradicts the overvaluation logic the proposal invokes, and the binary SIGN of a near-zero prstkc−sstk difference makes the moderator extremely noisy for the many firms with small offsetting option-related issuance.

EBITDA/EV and net total external financing are each established published anomalies and their SUMRANK is again purely additive, plus the "whole-capital" claim is undercut by scaling the financing leg by equity market cap rather than enterprise value.

This is a cosmetic three-year-smoothing variant of the first proposal in the same batch and overlaps directly with the known composite-issuance anomaly, so it adds a horizon tweak rather than a distinct economic mechanism.

The multiplicative structure is a legitimate conditional rather than an additive blend, but the stated reasoning is wrong about the expression's direction (a non-negative RANK multiplier makes expensive issuers the most *positive*, not most negative, scores) and the mechanical consequence is that the long leg is dominated by expensive repurchasers rather than cheap ones; additionally, raw csho growth is not split-adjusted and will generate spurious dilution readings.

The second leg is essentially Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing scaled by assets and the first is standard cash-flow-to-price, so this is an additive recombination of two known anomalies with no conditioning and heavy redundancy with the other five proposals in this batch.
